title: Resources: Direct Context, No Calls
objective: After this lesson you will be able to expose stable reference data as MCP resources (URIs, list/read), choose resources vs tools correctly, and design resource hierarchies that stay navigable as catalogs grow.
why: Not everything needs a function call: policy text, catalog snapshots, config files are *read directly* more cheaply than tool-mediated. Resources give clients addressable context (URIs) with list/read semantics — no argument schemas, no execution, no side effects. Misusing tools for static reads wastes latency and model reasoning on solved addressing.

blocks.text: Resources vs tools: address vs invoke

**Resources** expose data by URI (`policy://returns/30-day`, `catalog://products/SH-1`): list to discover, read to fetch — no arguments beyond the address, no execution, no side effects. **Tools** compute or act with validated arguments. Rule: stable reference content → resources; parameterized computation, live lookups, or actions → tools. Policy text as a resource; order lookup as a tool.

blocks.caption: URI-addressed context: discover, read, cite — never executed

blocks.text: URI schemes encode navigation: `catalog://category/shoes`, `catalog://product/SH-1`, `policy://returns/30-day`. List operations stay bounded per level (categories list products; products don't list the catalog). Templates (`catalog://product/{sku}`) address infinite spaces finitely. Flat single-level URI dumps become unlistable past dozens of entries — hierarchy is pagination by design.

Resources can stale silently (policy edited, resource cached): mitigate with versioned URIs or versions in metadata (`policy://returns/30-day@v14`), short TTLs on lists where supported, and as-of dates inside content (the RAG staleness discipline, applied to MCP). Clients should display provenance (URI + version) with cited content — citations need addresses.

blocks.title: Route address-vs-invoke
blocks.note: Run it: expect 4/4. Stable-addressable reads become URIs; computed/live/acting needs become tools. The routing question precedes every MCP addition.

items: Resources: URI-addressed stable context (list/read), no args, no effects; tools: computed/live/actions
Hierarchical URI schemes with templates scale; flat dumps don't; versions + as-of dates fight staleness
Route every addition by access pattern before building

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice router and confirm 4/4. (b) Design URIs for: returns policy v14, product SH-1, category shoes listing — with scheme rationale per URI. (c) State which gets a tool instead among: live inventory count, shipping-rate calc, refund issuance — with one-line reasons.
hints: Baseline 4/4; each case exercises one routing rule (stable-addressable vs computed/live/acting).
policy://returns/v14 (versioned!), catalog://product/SH-1, catalog://category/shoes — hierarchy + versions + templates.
All three are tools (live/computed/acting); resources would stale or side-effect. One line each names the disqualifier.
exercise.why: Access-pattern routing (address vs invoke) plus URI design (hierarchy, versions, templates) are the two resource judgments — each practiced on concrete catalog needs.
exercise.code: // Addition-router pattern: stable+addressable → resource; else tool.

quiz.q: Policy text via tool call with no arguments. Verdict?
options: Misuse: stable reference reads belong as URI-addressed resources — tools add latency, reasoning, and failure modes to solved addressing
quiz.explain: Address beats invocation for static content: list/read semantics, no schemas, no execution. Tools are for computed/live/acting needs.

quiz.q: 200 products in one flat resource listing. Problem + fix?
options: Unnavigable past dozens: hierarchical URIs (category → product) with templates bound the listing per level
quiz.explain: Hierarchy is pagination by design; flat dumps don't scale. Templates address infinite spaces finitely.

quiz.q: Cached policy resource edited upstream. Mitigations?
options: Versioned URIs + short TTLs + as-of dates in content + provenance display — staleness fought on four fronts
quiz.explain: Silent staleness corrupts answers citing old policy. Versions, TTLs, dates, and displayed provenance keep freshness auditable.

summary: Address stable context (hierarchical versioned URIs); invoke computed/live/acting needs (tools). Route by access pattern, never habit.
